From e0d4675789499b5955aa05ef9abc2926b30ba4ba Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Karel Zak <kzak@redhat.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Apr 2014 11:29:09 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] kill: fix bug in --all semantic

Introduces by 2ab6683f59cd3371b1c3ac8b5c248d5104ed4d41.

Signed-off-by: Karel Zak <kzak@redhat.com>

diff --git a/misc-utils/kill.c b/misc-utils/kill.c
index 37f4c6e34..d461b36a6 100644
--- a/misc-utils/kill.c
+++ b/misc-utils/kill.c
@@ -486,7 +486,7 @@ int main(int argc, char **argv)
 
 			if (!ps)
 				continue;
-			if (ctl.check_all)
+			if (!ctl.check_all)
 				proc_processes_filter_by_uid(ps, getuid());
 
 			proc_processes_filter_by_name(ps, ctl.arg);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `misc-utils/kill.c`**
- The condition checking for `ctl.check_all` was modified from `if (ctl.check_all)` to `if (!ctl.check_all)`. This change alters the logic to filter processes by user ID only when `check_all` is false, instead of when it is true.

### Relationships
- The modification in `kill.c` addresses a bug introduced by a previous commit (identified by the hash `2ab6683f59cd3371b1c3ac8b5c248d5104ed4d41`). The change ensures that the process filtering behavior aligns correctly with the intended semantics of the `--all` option, thereby fixing the bug related to how processes are filtered based on user ID when the `--all` flag is used.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
if (ctl.check_all)
    proc_processes_filter_by_uid(ps, getuid());
```
Reason:
The original condition checks if `ctl.check_all` is true, which incorrectly filters processes by user ID even when the `--all` option is specified. This leads to unintended behavior where not all processes are listed when the `--all` flag is active.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (!ctl.check_all)
    proc_processes_filter_by_uid(ps, getuid());
```
Reason:
The fix changes the condition to check if `ctl.check_all` is false, ensuring that user ID filtering only occurs when the `--all` option is not active. This allows all processes to be listed correctly when the `--all` flag is used.
